title: Choreography Timeline Director
description: The user directs a synchronized dance performance between Michelle and a flock of flamingos on a stage. Using a multi-track timeline editor, the user assigns animation clips to time slots, adjusts playback speeds, and couples character movements so that total stage energy (sum of all animation speeds) is conserved. Full undo/redo support lets the user refine the choreography.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Michelle.glb (skinned mesh with animation clips) and flamingo.glb (morph target bird animation). Place Michelle at center stage on a reflective plane. Instantiate 3 flamingo clones in a semicircle behind her, each with independent AnimationMixers. Add a hemisphere light, a warm spotlight on Michelle, and a cool directional light on the flamingos. Camera starts at a 30-degree elevated angle looking at stage center. Build an HTML/CSS overlay timeline panel at the bottom with 4 horizontal tracks (1 for Michelle, 3 for flamingos). Each track has 6 time slots the user can click to toggle animation on/off for that slot. Implement a CONSERVATION LAW: total animation energy equals 12 units. Each active slot costs 1 energy unit at normal speed. A speed slider per track (0.5x-2.0x) multiplies energy cost, so activating a slot at 2x costs 2 units. Display a real-time energy budget bar. When budget is exceeded, the last change is auto-rejected with a visual flash warning. Implement MULTI-INPUT COUPLING: when Michelle's track has 3+ active slots, all flamingo animations automatically sync their timeScale to match Michelle's slider value, shown by a chain-link icon. The user can break coupling by clicking the icon. Add UNDO/REDO with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y (minimum 20-step history) tracking all slot toggles, slider changes, and coupling toggles. Show undo/redo buttons in the UI with step counters. Add a Play button that scrubs through the timeline, playing each character's mixer only during their active slots at their assigned speed. During playback, highlight the current time column. Include a Reset button that restores default state (all slots off, sliders at 1x, full energy). The stage floor should subtly pulse with a color mapped to current energy usage percentage.
